subject: Archaeology
title: Plague DNA: Ancient Pandemics
description: A quick, practical guide to Plague DNA: Ancient Pandemics.

hook.text: Scientists pulled plague DNA from 5,000-year-old teeth. The killer bacterium is ancient.

buildup.text: Yersinia pestis has been found in remains across Eurasia dating back to 3000 BCE.

discovery.text: Early strains lacked flea transmission genes. They spread person-to-person, not through rats.

twist.text: A plague pandemic may explain mysterious population crashes in Neolithic Europe.

climax.text: Tracking plague evolution helps predict how future pandemics might emerge.

punchline.text: The plague is 5,000 years old. Teeth trapped the evidence.

quiz.question: What did ancient plague DNA reveal about early strains?
options: They were far more lethal than the medieval Black Death
Early forms lacked flea transmission and spread person-to-person
The bacterium came from the Americas and was carried east
